The small-time stationary velocity has sixth cumulant v⁶p(1−15p+30p²); solving its upper zero yields the exact h/a threshold. Continuity forces a sixth-cumulant crossing above threshold. Separate exact algebra and finite-time matrix ODE checks passed 33 assertions; tests are not substituted for proof.

originality.rationale: The directly comparable prior three-phase source by Santra, Olsen and Gupta (arXiv:2408.16643, Section 4.2, equation (54)) gives fourth-order position cumulants and a general transform. The fourth-cumulant-neutral surface therefore receives no novelty credit. A fresh exact eighth-order tilted-eigenvalue analysis establishes the strictly opposite sixth/eighth long-time growth signs at fourth-neutrality; a stationary instantaneous-velocity calculation additionally proves a sharp sufficient parameter threshold for an unavoidable finite-time sixth-cumulant reversal. These combined higher-order sign and finite-time conclusions were not identified in the inspected prior texts or accessible claim records. The published general transform can in principle be differentiated to reach the higher rates, so implicit coverage remains an explicit residual priority risk.

value.rationale: The exact fourth-neutral tuning in intermittent active matter is a natural experiment where kurtosis ceases to detect the leading non-Gaussian fluctuation rate. The sixth and eighth rate signs prove the signal persists, and the sharp short-time-sign threshold forces a measurable sixth-order transient reversal without modifying variance. The result is a structural diagnosis of apparent Gaussianity and hidden active/rest dynamics, not an arbitrary high-order coefficient table. Generality is restricted to stated Markov rates and stationary initialization.
